pr_title: DualStack: basic dual-stack node IP handling
pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**
/kind feature

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
Makes two related improvements to kubelet node IP handling:

- On bare metal (ie, when there is no `--cloud-provider`), the administrator can now pass a comma-separated pair of IPs via `--node-ip` to manually configure dual-stack `node.status.addresses`. No other scenarios (eg, cloud provider, bare-metal autodetection) are changed.
- On nodes with dual-stack `node.status.addresses` (regardless of how they got them), hostNetwork pods will now have dual-stack `pod.status.podIPs`, allowing the pod to be the target of either a single-stack IPv4 or single-stack IPv6 Service (or, once #91824 merges, a dual-stack Service).

There is ongoing discussion about dual-stack node IPs in https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/1665, and it probably won't be resolved in time for Enhancement Freeze. However, it seems like there has always been consensus that (a) regardless of what else is possible, it ought to be possible to explicitly specify a dual-stack pair of IPs on bare-metal nodes, (b) regardless of how a node ends up with dual-stack IPs, if it has dual-stack IPs, then that should be reflected in hostNetwork pods. So this PR implements those two things. Additional functionality will presumably come later.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes #91940
Fixes #89816 (invalid node IP set by cloud provider causes `"<nil>"` podIP on hostnetwork pod)

**Special notes for your reviewer**:
Currently built on top of #94474 (the first two commits). That can still be reviewed separately, or it can be reviewed as part of this.

Does not conflict with #91824 (dual-stack Services), as this PR only touches kubelet-related things, and that PR does not touch anything kubelet related except a small fix to kubenet (which this PR doesn't touch).

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:
```release-note
In dual-stack bare-metal clusters, you can now pass dual-stack IPs to `kubelet --node-ip`.
eg: `kubelet --node-ip 10.1.0.5,fd01::0005`. This is not yet supported for non-bare-metal
clusters.

In dual-stack clusters where nodes have dual-stack addresses, hostNetwork pods
will now get dual-stack PodIPs.
```

/sig network
/sig node
/priority important-soon
/assign @thockin

issue_context.title: unexpected podIP and hostIP in pod
issue_context.body:
**What happened**:

Unexpected podIP and hostIP in pod, just like
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: test
  namespace: test
spec:
  containers:
  ......
status:
  ......
  hostIP: <nil>
  podIP: <nil>
  ......
```

**What you expected to happen**:

This is a host-networking pod, podIP and hostIP in status should be node's internal IP.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

Set kubelet's cloud provider to `external`, then set some invalid addresses to node.


**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):  1.14

Order is assumed here. Which is fine if we know that the node.Status.Addresses is always ordered correctly. is this confirmed?

This function is what defines what "ordered correctly" is for node.Status.Addresses. Whatever IP the cloud provider returns first is the one that kubelet will use.

Note that the first IP returned here is the same as was traditionally returned by the old single-value `GetNodeHostIP()`; "the first InternalIP, unless there are no InternalIPs, in which case the first ExternalIP". I just changed the way it figures that out because with dual-stack we need to do that logic twice so it's easier to just sort the IPs correctly beforehand.
